translations.text: Hear, dearest children, the rule of the faith, which you must keep mindfully in your hearts, you who have received the Christian name,
that is, the token of your Christianity, breathed into men by the Lord and established by his own disciples.
Of this faith there are indeed few words, but very great mysteries are contained in them.
Indeed, the Holy Spirit dictated these words with such brevity to the masters of Christianity, his holy apostles,
so that what all Christians must believe and also always confess, all might understand and keep in memory.
How then does a man call himself a Christian who [does not learn] these few words of the faith, by which he shall be saved and by which he shall be healed, and also the words of the Lord's Prayer,
which the Lord himself gave and established as law? How can he be a Christian who will not learn them or keep them in his memory?
Or how can he stand surety in the faith for another, or make a promise on behalf of another, who does not yet know the faith himself?
Therefore you must know, my little children, that until each one of you has taught that same faith to his godchild, so that the godchild understands it,
the godchild whom he receives from baptism, he is guilty against God's promise; and he who neglects to teach his godchild shall give account on the Day of Judgment.
Now let every man who wishes to be a Christian hasten with all eagerness to learn the faith and the Lord's Prayer, and also to teach them to those whom he receives from baptism,
so that he is not compelled to give account on the Day of Judgment. For it is God's command, and it is our salvation and our Lord's command, and we cannot otherwise obtain forgiveness of our sins.
